question: Why does a Next.js Root Layout preserve interactive state (such as a reader note or audio player) when navigating from `/` to `/articles/rsc-guide`?
options: Layouts do not re-mount during client-side navigations between sibling routes; only the nested page segment swaps
Next.js saves all component state inside cookies on every click
Next.js reloads the entire HTML document on every Link click
React disables useState inside page.tsx files
explanation: In the App Router, layout.tsx wraps child page segments and stays mounted across route transitions, preserving local client state inside the layout shell.

question: Why should generateStaticParams(), generateMetadata(), and sitemap.ts all read from the same data access module (data.ts)?
options: To force every article page into dynamic rendering on every request
So static build paths, page <title> tags, and /sitemap.xml URLs always stay synchronized with one canonical source of truth
Because Next.js forbids importing functions from more than one file
To expose raw database connection credentials to browser components
explanation: Sharing one data layer ensures static routes, metadata titles, and XML sitemaps reflect the exact same set of published articles without drift.

question: Which ARIA attribute should a persistent NavBar apply to the link matching the user's current route?
explanation: aria-current='page' is the standard accessibility attribute indicating which navigation link represents the currently active page.

question: What should an article detail route render when matchBlogRoute('/articles/unknown') extracts a slug that returns null from getPostBySlug()?
options: The first article in the database instead
A clear not-found screen with a link back to the home article list
explanation: When a requested slug does not exist in the data store, rendering a dedicated not-found state (like calling notFound() in Next.js) gives users a clear recovery path.
